newsitem.title: USA: Republicans promise action on tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Republicans promise action on tax cuts.

text.p: Republicans in Congress will press for permanent tax cuts as part of their legislative agenda to improve the quality of life for Americans, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Saturday.

"We're ready to bring about the changes America needs," Lott said in the Republican response to President Clinton's weekly radio address. Republicans control both the Senate and House of Representatives.
"For Republicans, those changes aim at a better quality of life for all Americans, and it starts with your home, your work place, your neighbourhood," the Mississippi lawmaker said.
"It starts with our belief that government should take less of what you earn, and that you should keep more of it. In other words, permanent tax relief.

"The decisions you and millions of other individual Americans make about spending and saving and investing are the best way to foster economic growth, higher take-home pay and greater opportunity for everyone," Lott added. He did not give any details on how big a tax cut Republicans would propose.

Lott said Republicans would also act quickly on a constitutional amendment requiring Congress to pass a balanced federal budget each year. The amendment passed the House two years ago but failed by one vote in the Senate.

"We know that most Americans want government to stop piling up a mountain of debt for tommorrow's youngsters to face the rest of their lives. That's why we're promising early action on a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution. It will safeguard the future of the American family," he said.

Lott said other Republican goals included legislation on education, health care and crime. "We want every child to have a chance for a good education in a school free from violence and drugs, like my own children had."
He said another bill would give workers more options for expanded leave time to be with their families.
